subject: Post-demo: Redwood vs Hyperscaler - reranking & embeddings perf + next tests
messages:

Subject: Post-demo: Redwood vs Hyperscaler - reranking & embeddings perf + next tests

Hi Sam / Jane,

Great to meet yesterday — thanks again for the time and for walking through your current search stack. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can make the comparison vs the hyperscaler concrete:

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary goal: improve freshness & relevance for product search (reduce false positives in top-10).
- Current stack: embeddings + vector DB (managed hyperscaler solution) for retrieval, followed by a lightweight reranker.
- Constraints: 200ms target end-to-end retrieval + reranking for web queries, budget target ~ $0.0008/query at 1M qps/month.

What Redwood will run for evaluation
1) Retrieval-only baseline: embeddings at 1536 dims (Open models) + FAISS-style index on single node (measure recall@K, vector latency).
2) Retrieval + lightweight rerank: 1-2 layer transformer reranker on top of top-50 results (measure recall@10, nDCG, CPU/GPU cost).
3) Our hybrid: prefix caching + quantized embeddings (8-bit) to test cost/latency trade-offs and fallback path.

Metrics we'll capture
- Retrieval latency (p50/p95) per query and per satellite (region).
- Recall@K and recall@10 / nDCG against your golden labels.
- Cost per query (tokens + embedding storage + rerank compute).
- Index memory footprint and ops for incremental updates.

Proposed next steps
- You share a representative sample (we've attached a sample queries CSV template) + golden labels.
- Redwood runs the 3 test variants above and returns a short benchmark PDF with per-query breakdowns.
- Joint sync after results to pick the final PoC config and any SLA/contract questions.

Can you confirm: 1) the sample CSV is okay, 2) do you have constraints on embedding dim (if you must stay at 768 for compatibility), and 3) who should be included from procurement for contract/PO discussions?

Thanks — I'll loop in Vivek for the engineering test-plan details.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132

2) Embedding dim: we currently use 768 in prod for downstream compatibility but can test 1536 for the evaluation if that helps. We care most about recall@10 and end-to-end 95th percentile latency.
3) Procurement point: procurement@acme-corp.com — cc'ing them on future contract threads.

Also looping in Jane to make sure this matches your goals.

—Sam

Hi Sam — thanks for the quick replies. I put together a short test-plan and expected numbers so you can set expectations internally. See attached `redwood-vs-hyperscaler-test-plan.md` and summarized below.

Short answers to your asks:
- Reranker latency overhead:
  - GPU (T4/A10 class): expected rerank p95 for top-50 ~ 20-40ms depending on model size (small 2-layer ~20ms, medium ~35ms).
  - CPU (8-16 cores x86): expected p95 ~ 150-400ms for the same reranker; we recommend GPU if you need sub-200ms E2E.
- Private deployment: Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) supports data residency in your VPC; we can run entirely on customer-managed infra with KMS/HSM integrations. No data egress required for inference unless you elect to send logs to our control plane for observability.

Suggested evaluation config (we'll run all three variants):
A) Hyperscaler baseline (what you currently run): embedding dim 768, managed vector DB, retrieval p95 ~ 60-120ms (varies by region), recall@10 measured vs provided labels. We'll instrument to validate your current numbers.
B) Redwood retrieval-only: 1536 dim (optional), quantized to 8-bit vectors for storage/computation test, vector query p95 target 20-40ms on our optimized runtime, recall@10 expected +/- 2-3% vs 768 depending on model.
C) Redwood retrieval + rerank: same embedding pipeline + a 2-layer transformer reranker on top-50. Expected impact: recall@10 + nDCG improvements in 5-12% range for product search queries from our prior benchmarks; E2E p95 depends on reranker placement (GPU recommended).

Data we need from you
- Sample queries + gold labels (10k rows) — you mentioned you'll send Friday.
- Typical sequence length and any heavy metadata we should index (skus, category).
- Rough QPS distribution so we can size the test runner and simulate load.

Deliverables after test run (72–96h turnaround after we receive data)
- Per-query CSV with scores from each variant + latency columns.
- Aggregate metrics: recall@K, recall@10, nDCG, p50/p95 latencies, cost per query estimate.
- Short recommendation note: configuration we’d pick for PoC (model, quantization, batching).

Differentiators vs hyperscalers we’ll validate in the report
- Consistent p95s due to runtime optimizations (kernel selection + KV caching).
- Cost-per-query with quantized embeddings and intelligent batching (we'll show sample cost model).
- Deployment flexibility: can run in your VPC with identical API and rollout controls.

If that aligns, we'll schedule a 30-min sync next week to walk the results and decide on PoC. Suggest Tue 2/24 or Wed 2/25.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
